title: A performance refactor of AdminPermission.projects split one combined Q filter into chained .filter(teams__members=user).filter(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS) calls, so read-only team members get admin rights on any project that also belongs to some admin team.

findings.explanation: No raw SQL queries are introduced. The change refactors Django ORM filter calls using Q objects, which are parameterized by the ORM framework. No user-controlled input is passed directly into a SQL string.

This change is a security fix, not a vulnerability introduction. The previous code chained separate .filter() calls on related models, which produced independent JOINs and could return projects where the user is a member of ANY team, as long as SOME (possibly different) team had admin access. Combining the conditions into a single Q object ensures both conditions apply to the same JOIN, correctly enforcing that the user must be a member of a team that has the required access level.

evidence.content:
+            team_filters = Q(teams__members=user)
             if admin and not member:
-                projects_from_teams = projects_from_teams.filter(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS)
+                team_filters &= Q(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS)
             elif member and not admin:
-                projects_from_teams = projects_from_teams.filter(teams__access=READ_ONLY_ACCESS)
+                team_filters &= Q(teams__access=READ_ONLY_ACCESS)
